name: Edward L. Simmers
role: Medora schoolteacher and Billings County probate judge
bio: Edward L. Simmers opened school in Medora hall at the end of November 1885 with 22 pupils, which grew to 26, and the paper praised his teaching and his system of class rankings. In March 1886 he was added to the Billings County ticket as a candidate for probate judge, and that April he took charge of the N. P. Hotel bar in Medora. By October 1886 he was Probate Judge Simmers, when he left for a business opening in Chicago.

The school is in flourishing condition, and praises of Mr. Simmers' instruction are numerous. There are now twenty-six scholars in attendance. A night school is conductec in addition.
Much good scholarship is being aroused by teacher Simmers, in a competitive system of rank in classes.
